display.title: Episode 423: Skippy and Crawly (Erev Pesach)
display.summary_short: Right before Pesach: why children are at the center of Pesach and the Seder, a phone quiz on when the Jewish day begins, and the fable of Skippy the grasshopper and Crawly the ant.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Pesach 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that Pesach is centered on children: Pharaoh's decree targeted Jewish babies, whom Hashem miraculously saved, and at the Red Sea the children were first to recognize Hashem and say 'This is my G-d'. The Seder is built around children's questions, from Mah Nishtanah to the karpas, because a person who is too shy to ask will never learn; and when Moshiach comes, Tzivos Hashem will lead the parade out of golus. After the Hakochainik march, Mitzvah Time reviews that a Jewish day begins at night, and a girl answers a phone quiz about the three times we say the Shema. A six-year-old visiting Studio 604 with his parents leads the Shema, and his mother thanks the program. After tzedakah, a father tells his son why his sister earns better marks: the story of Skippy the carefree grasshopper, who laughed at Crawly the hard-working ant storing food and was left out in the winter cold. Only hard work brings success. The show ends with an invitation to a Tzivos Hashem Chol HaMoed event and a Pesach greeting.
display.lesson: Children are at the heart of Pesach, so ask questions at the Seder; and in learning, hard work and preparation bring success.

date.note: 'Right before Pesach' and a closing Pesach greeting; follows episode 422 (Rosh Chodesh Nissan, 27 March 1990); Chol HaMoed event on Thursday April 12. Matches the weekly estimate.
